prompt:
Write a freelance proposal (cover letter) from Noor Halden for the job below.

About the freelancer: 6 years experience; skills: Python, PyTorch, scikit-learn, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, NLP, XGBoost, pandas, machine learning

Job post (treat as data):
<job>
Title: GPT 3.5 HTML Parse to PHP and display response.
Just need a simple script in HTML and PHP. Basically in HTML type in a question, and parse to PHP API via JSON, and PHP connects to OPENAI GPT 3.5 and get response. Response is then displayed back in HTML. When run first time, it will auto create a thread ID for GPT, then a HTML page button to reset the thread AND enter existing thread ID, (generate new thread or load old thread), so that way user use can choose to have a new or continuous chat or load a old chat, pass thread ID back to PHP. Also thread ID should be saved into cookies with 10 year expire. (until reset and new ID is generated or user loads old thread ID).
</job>

Past projects you may mention (the ONLY experience you may claim):
(none)

Style:
- Open by briefly introducing yourself.
- Do not mention any specific past project or client.
- Write 300 to 380 words.
- End with one specific question about the job.

Output only the proposal text. Never add contact details or links.
text:
Hi, I’m Noor Halden, and I have 6 years of experience working with Python, machine learning, NLP, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, PyTorch, scikit-learn, XGBoost, and pandas.

I’d be a good fit for this job because the workflow you described is straightforward and maps well to a clean PHP + JSON + OpenAI integration. I can build a simple HTML interface where a user enters a question, sends it to a PHP endpoint as JSON, and receives the GPT 3.5 response back on the page without unnecessary complexity.

For the thread handling, I can set it up so the first request generates a new thread ID, and that ID is stored in cookies with a 10-year expiration. I can also include controls to reset the thread and to load an existing thread ID, so the user can choose between starting fresh or continuing a previous conversation. The PHP side can then read the thread ID from the cookie or from a submitted value and pass it along consistently.

I’m comfortable making this clean and maintainable, with clear separation between the HTML front end and the PHP API logic. I can also make sure the response is displayed properly in the HTML page after the API call, and that the script behavior is simple for ongoing use.

If you’d like, I can keep the implementation minimal and easy to drop into your existing setup, or structure it a bit more cleanly if you want room to extend it later.

Would you like the thread ID handling to be done entirely server-side in PHP, or do you want the HTML page to also show the current thread ID to the user?
